text: Manchester United are tracking Argentina midfielder Nico Paz, 22, ahead of a potential move next summer. Paz scored twice for Como against United in the Champions League last month. ( Sun )
New United manager Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window, with United likely to be in the market for a defender and a striker. ( Telegraph )
Barcelona are willing to sanction the January sale of France international Jules Kounde, 28, who is a target for Chelsea . ( Teamtalk )

Spanish giants Real Madrid are also keen on signing 18-year-old Brazilian defender Vitao from Atletico Mineiro, with Brighton and Everton also interested. ( Sport - in Spanish ).
Barcelona are another club keeping tabs on teenage centre-back Vitao. ( Teamtalk )

However, Zubimendi says he is "happy" in London and surprised by the rumours about his future as he has not contacted anyone about a move. (Marca - in Spanish)

Manchester United have added Brentford and Republic of Ireland centre-back Nathan Collins, 25, and Fulham 's 26-year-old Nigeria international Calvin Bassey to their list of potential defensive targets, which also includes Everton and England defender Jarrad Branthwaite, 24. (Mail - subscription required)

The Gunners face competition from Roma and Sporting for Endrick, who are both keen to take him on loan until the end of the season with the player not yet ready to give up on his Real Madrid career. (AS - in Spanish)

Manchester United have added Brentford 's Republic of Ireland centre-back Nathan Collins, 25, and Fulham 's Nigeria defender Calvin Bassey, 26, to their list of possible January targets. (Mail - subscription required)

Dutch left-back Ian Maatsen, 24, Argentine winger Emiliano Buendia, 29, Belgium midfielder Amadou Onana, 25, and English midfielder Ross Barkley, 32, are all set to sign new contracts with Aston Villa in the near future. (Telegraph - subscription required)

However, USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino, who managed Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, is the new bookmakers' favourite to replace Carrick at Old Trafford. (Standard)
